skill.name: batch-job-runner
skill.description: Enrich existing contact lists through Leadsets in batches sized to your account limits. Save progress between batches and group results by work email status.
skill.summary: Plan, checkpoint, and resume Leadsets contact enrichment within account limits.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets MCP endpoint is an intended external dependency that receives contact identifiers during enrichment. The other 21 alerts do not show shell execution, environment access, host reconnaissance, or automatic requests to the linked pages. The workflow can write checkpoints before approval, submit identifiers without a clear scope check, and replay paid calls after the documented retry period.

remediation.issue: The default checkpoint can modify the source list before approval.
remediation.suggestion: Keep planning read-only and default to a separate checkpoint. Confirm the destination before modifying the input file, shared sheet, or CRM.

remediation.issue: The workflow does not require clear approval for every enrichment scope.
remediation.suggestion: Before the first enrichment request, confirm Leadsets, the fields to send, and maximum record usage unless the user already approved that scope.

remediation.issue: A saved checkpoint can lag behind completed, billable requests.
remediation.suggestion: Persist each request outcome as it arrives. Reconcile unresolved requests before retrying after the 24-hour window, and qualify the no-double-charge claim.

semantic_findings.title: Source Checkpoint Can Be Written Before Approval
semantic_findings.description: The default checkpoint adds a status column to the input and places a log beside it. This can modify a shared source before approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The first step adds the status column. The confirmation step comes later and applies only to jobs spanning more than one window.

semantic_findings.title: Approval Does Not Cover Every Enrichment Scope
semantic_findings.description: Single-window runs can submit contact identifiers to Leadsets and consume account quota without confirming the data scope and cost when the user request is unclear.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow requests approval only for multi-window jobs, then sends a real enrichment probe. A single-window request can already be authorized, but scope is not checked.

semantic_findings.title: Resumed Batches Can Repeat Billable Requests
semantic_findings.description: An interruption before a batch checkpoint can leave completed requests marked pending. Retrying them after the documented 24-hour protection can consume quota again.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow saves progress after each batch and states a 24-hour retry guarantee. It does not describe reconciliation of unresolved requests before a later resume.

content.value_statement: Large contact lists can exceed your Leadsets quota before the job finishes. This skill plans batches around available quota, saves progress, and groups results by email status.
actual_capabilities: Deduplicate existing contacts by LinkedIn URL, email, or name and company domain.
Check the current and weekly Leadsets allowances before planning batches.
Test input field mapping with a small enrichment probe.
Save progress after each batch and use the checkpoint to skip completed rows.
Report batch progress, records used, and available reset times.
Group results by email status and include a run log.
limitations: Requires a Leadsets account and either an MCP connection or REST API access.
Sheet and CRM access depend on connections available to the agent.
Background execution or automatic restart depends on the agent environment.
The skill enriches existing rows only. It does not find new contacts or send email.

use_cases.title: Plan a Large CRM Enrichment Job
use_cases.description: Estimate how many Leadsets windows an exported contact list needs and compare the estimate with your weekly allowance.

use_cases.title: Resume an Interrupted Client Batch
use_cases.description: Use the saved checkpoint and account usage to continue processing rows that are still pending.

use_cases.title: Review Email Status Groups
use_cases.description: Separate verified, catch-all, unknown, and missing emails before deciding which records to import.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate the Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Plan without sending contact data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check Leadsets usage and estimate batches for this CSV. Keep the file unchanged and do not send contact data.

prompt_templates.title: Probe One Contact
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Confirm which input columns map to Leadsets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the marked row for a Leadsets enrichment probe. Summarize the field mapping and returned work email status without printing the email.

prompt_templates.title: Run with a Weekly Ceiling
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Process an approved list within a budget.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this batch with a 40% weekly usage ceiling and a separate checkpoint. Confirm the fields to send and the record budget before processing. Export results as CSV.

prompt_templates.title: Resume from a Saved Checkpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Review pending work after an interruption.
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile the checkpoint with the run log and refresh Leadsets usage. Resume only confirmed pending rows. Ask before replaying any request with an unknown outcome.

output_examples.input: Estimate the run for an approved contact list without submitting any rows.
output_examples.output: The list has 1,150 unique rows after duplicates were removed. It needs at least two usage windows. No contact rows were submitted.

output_examples.input: Report progress after a rate limit pauses an approved batch.
output_examples.output: Processed 360 of 900 rows and saved the checkpoint. This window used 330 enrichment records. The service reports a reset at 14:15 UTC.

output_examples.input: Summarize the finished batch without exposing email addresses.
output_examples.output: The CSV export contains separate files for verified, catch-all, unknown, and missing emails. The run log lists record usage, pauses, and errors.

best_practices: Confirm the Leadsets destination, permitted fields, and record budget before sending any contacts.
Use a separate checkpoint and save it in a location approved for contact data.
Refresh account usage and review uncertain requests before resuming a paused run.
anti_patterns: Overwrite a CRM or shared sheet without confirming the destination and scope.
Treat catch-all or unknown emails as verified.
Replay every pending row after an interruption without checking which requests may already have succeeded.

faq.question: Which input formats can I use?
faq.answer: Use a CSV, Google Sheet tab, or CRM export. Each row needs a LinkedIn URL, a name and company domain, or an existing work email.

faq.question: Does enrichment send data to Leadsets?
faq.answer: Yes. Enrichment sends contact identifiers from selected rows through the configured Leadsets connection. Share only fields you are authorized to send.

faq.question: How does the skill choose batch sizes?
faq.answer: The default uses up to 500 rows or the remaining five-hour allowance after a 10% buffer, whichever is smaller.

faq.question: What happens when the account reaches a limit?
faq.answer: The workflow can retry a short rate-limit delay or pause with a checkpoint and reset time. Exhausted free records do not refill.

faq.question: Can it resume automatically after I close my session?
faq.answer: The workflow saves a checkpoint for resuming. An automatic restart requires an agent environment that supports background execution or scheduling.

faq.question: Does it send emails or write results back to my CRM?
faq.answer: It does not send email. Results default to CSV. CRM write-back requires an available connection and should be explicitly authorized.
